title: Stream reconnect safeguards, partial-generation compaction, and tool-call resume safety
text:
Stream reconnect safeguards, partial-generation compaction, and tool-call resume safety

description:
Problem: Clients frequently disconnect mid-generation (mobile flaps, browser refreshes, network NAT timeouts). Partial outputs, especially when function/tool calls are involved or when structured outputs are being streamed, can leave server-side resources (KV cache state, ephemeral prefixes, inflight function handles) in inconsistent states. Current heuristics aggressively GC or keep long-lived leases, causing either data loss for legitimate reconnects or resource exhaustion under scale.

Goal: Implement a multi-tiered reconnection and compaction strategy that balances availability for reconnects, resource cost, and correctness for function/tool-call sequences and structured output streams. Provide observable signals in the Console and safe compatibility shims for older SDKs.

acceptance_criteria:
Reconnect handshake with resume-token validation implemented and enabled behind feature flag
Partial-generation compaction that coalesces ephemeral prefix fragments into a single resumable snapshot when safe
Function/tool-call tokens are pinned until either an ACK or definitive TTL expiration; tool side-effects are not re-invoked on resume unless idempotency key present
GC policy microbench shows <= 5% additional memory overhead at p95 with 0.5% decrease in throughput under load compared to baseline
Console exposes per-session resume attempts, orphaned-generation counts, and GC churn metrics
Graceful fallback policy: when resume fails, clients receive deterministic finalization payload (partial + truncated markers) instead of ambiguous EOF

tasks:
Design: define resume-token format compatible with current SDKs and legacy clients
Server: implement lease epochs and tombstone markers for orphaned generations
Runtime: compact ephemeral prefix fragments to resumable snapshots when no cross-request function calls depend on missing context
Function-calling safety: implement idempotency-key pinning and tool-handle tombstones
API: add streaming response fields 'resume_token' and 'finalization_reason' to structured output spec
E2E tests: flaky reconnect emulator (packet loss, reconnect after 2s, 30s, 5m), function call replay protection
Instrumentation: Console dashboard widgets and alerts for orphaned-generation ratio and GC latency
Rollout: gated feature flag, gradual rollout to 5% -> 25% -> 100% with monitor-based rollback

implementation_notes:
Resume-token format is opaque base64; servers validate HMAC with rotating key-store. SDKs will expose 'can_resume' boolean after initial handshake.
Compaction runs only when: (1) no outstanding function handles pinned to older fragments, (2) fragment count > 3, or (3) memory pressure threshold crossed
Tool-call pinning avoids re-invoking side-effects. If idempotency key absent and resume attempts > 1, server will finalise with 'incomplete_function_call' marker and surface link to logs
Backward compatibility: old SDKs receive resume_token but cannot auto-resume; add client library version gated behavior with runtime fallback to 'deterministic finalization'

observability_playbook:
Dashboard: Console -> Streaming -> Resume attempts (success/fail)
Alert: orphaned-generation-rate > 0.5% for 10m -> pager
SLO: resume-success-rate >= 99.5% for P50 reconnect window (<= 30s)
Logging: emit event with resume_token_hash, session_id, reason (disconnect|timeout|client_abort)

comments:
2026-03-05 - Ava Martinez: Created ticket after incident TRE-2026-03 where multiple mobile clients lost partial generations following aggressive 30s TTL sweep. Linked incident notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/INC/TRE-2026-03
2026-03-07 - Sahil Kapoor: Spike complete. Prototype resume-token uses (session_id, seq, epoch, hmac). Trade-offs: longer tokens surface runtime internals; decided to HMAC and include only opaque base64 in API. Spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4387
2026-03-09 - Design review (Marta Li): UX needs clear client-facing deterministic finalization state. Proposed payload shape and 'truncated' marker for structured output. Drive design doc: https://drive.google.com/designs/stream-resume-ux
2026-03-10 - Eng sync: Decided pinning policy: function-call handles are pinned for min(ack_ttl, 5m) and extended to 24h only if client-supplied idempotency key present. Reason: reduce risk of replaying side-effects. Added task to docs and SDKs to add automatic idempotency-key wiring.
2026-03-11 - PR opened: runtime: lease-epochs and tombstone support. Initial implementation behind feature flag 'stream_resume_v2'. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4399
2026-03-12 - QA: E2E test failures when compacting ephemeral fragments with interleaved tool-calls. Root cause: compact algorithm assumed tool-call boundaries aligned with chunk boundaries. Action: update chunk metadata to include 'last_safe_tool_boundary' and re-run tests. Test flakiness ticket: ENG-884330
2026-03-13 - Performance: microbench against g4dn-like instance: p95 latency increase 3ms with compaction enabled, mem overhead +3% at steady state. Need further tuning; plan to offload compaction to background worker pool to spread CPU.
